html:
Origin and position

Hector is the only son of King Francis-Ilianus; he has sixteen sisters. (Francis-Ilian) When his father retired to the monastery at the bottomless failure, the affairs of the kingdom passed to the prince, and most of the courtiers moved to his court. (Bottomless Abyss) Hector himself said at the court of Minerva that "for ten years he has been conducting the affairs of the glorious South." Formally, as Iona noted, the prince could not make important decisions without the consent of his father, but in fact Shimmery himself ruled: he elevated several nobles - generals and counts who were in disgrace with his father - and removed his father's protégés from the court. The Shimmerians believed that Hector ruled "good" until he allowed the Shavans to beat himself.

In the Council of Five, which held the prey of spark eyes, the Fourth of the Five stood on the side of the Prince, while the Second (Abbot Count Quindar) and the Third held on to their father. With the Third of the Five, the "king of winemakers", Hector once befriended on the grounds of a love of pleasures, but stole his best althessa; since then, he has repeatedly urged the king-prophet to return to the throne.

At the court of Minerva, he was declared a full title: "Hector Elvira Adelaide of the genus Sophia Velichava, First of the Five, Baron of Marble Gorges, Earl of Astellit, honorary burgomaster of the White Stone Laem, Crown Prince of the Shimmery Kingdom." In the text, he is also called Hector Nellis-Lyon; in a royal marriage letter about his sister Demeter, the genus is called the "Great House of Nellis-Lyon".

In "Only One Star"

In the autumn of 1774, Adrian, having opposed Moran of the Steppe Fire, called the Shimmerians into allies. (Moran Steppe Fire) The embassy to Prince Adrian commissioned his advisor Catherine Catherine, Hector's former althesse: she sailed to Shimmery on the Lord's fastest corvette. Hector led three hundred and twenty ships, provided by Shimmery merchants and nobles, and an army to the pirate's bay midway from Faunterra to Litland; Catherine returned with him and was with the prince throughout the campaign. In Litland, she explained to the South that the horde had not retreated: the corpses nailed to the trees were executed deserters, and the West came for blood revenge. Adrian immediately took advantage of the Shimmerian fleet to send five of the eight spark regiments north, and Hector anxiously asked if the lord would go to Steppe Fire with three.

In Litland, the prince was self-confident and mocking: he promised to “liberate all to one” peasants, called himself the “famous savior of the rural rabble” and explained that the southerners are fighting with pleasure. When the intelligence found traces of the horde, Adrian ordered to remove the imperial banners and brought forward the Shimmerian regiments as bait. On December 2, the Day of Descent, at the dry bed of the Orange River on the road to Melorange, the horde struck directly into the Shimmerian avant-garde: the southerners did not last long and fled, after which the imperial spark infantry defeated the Shavans. About two and a half thousand Shimmerians were killed, another thousand were at death, although most of the fallen were mercenaries, not vassals of the prince. Manson mockingly "translated" his thoughts aloud: according to this "translation", the prince thinks that the lord deceived him and promised the Rings, - Adrian replied that the Rings did not promise. Going north, Adrian left Hector's army in Melorange - ostensibly to help the Litlands, in fact, to get rid of the risk of betrayal.

"A Doll on the Throne"

Melorange

In the winter of 1775, the prince held a defense in Melorange. Shavani called him a "semi-enemy": he was "not as vile as the Litlands, not as ferocious as the Northerners". After receiving an anonymous letter warning of Moran's infiltrators, Hector caught Naymir and Chara and interrogated them himself — theatrically, with pleasure, sitting in a framed chair in a hug with his girlfriend. (Neimir) Neymir called himself the Shimmer merchant Ney-Lukkum of Orkad and even tried to strangle the prince; under the threat of torture, he "confessed" that Moran wanted to burn the Shimmerian fleet in port and go to the defenseless Shimmery. Hector was delighted — "I, Hector of Shimmery, will end the horde. I will do what the great Adrian could not do!” and ordered the execution of the prisoners, leaving so that the spectacle would not spoil his appetite. Chara warned him that "the West has a long memory"; the prisoners were saved by a sorcerer.

Then the prince suddenly led the army out of the city by a rapid march eastward, to the Rain Forest, and the horde, striking the flank and rear, defeated the Shimmerians, capturing the entire convoy - silverware, silk, fruit and wine; the survivors fled to the ships. According to Shimmerian rumours, Steppe Fire sacrificed two of the best horsemen for this victory; the scouts themselves later said that Moran had sacrificed them "to outwit Prince Hector".

the Minerva Court

In the spring, the prince arrived in Faunterra from Laham, for the spring session of the House, with a huge entourage of generals, vassals, merchants and altess. (Chamber of Representatives) At the reception, Minerva pricked him with a question about his father's health, and Hector in response hinted at her dependence on Agatha. When she asked why the journey from Meloranzh took so long, it turned out that the defeat of the Crown knows nothing. The prince, whose face in anger "fell disfigured", becoming like a crow, assured that he had sent two pigeons and a courier, who was supposed to convey the letter by a wave from Marengo. Minerva later found out that the pigeons were intercepted by Erwin's men, and the message along the wave was detained by the Minister of Railways Liam Shelier, fearing that the mistress would leave with the army for Litland.

After the reception, the prince quickly became friends with Erwin on the basis of wine, dance and violass: they devoted the whole night to "getting acquainted with the culture and traditions of the Shimmery kingdom." Later, Hector warned Minerva about the perfidy of the Shavans and offered her an "elegant way" to break the Steppe Fire with the rest of the Shavans, and Erwin - to sell 15 thousand spark eyes. Minerva suspected that the prince had deliberately lost the battle and that he had violated the dynasty's monopoly by selling his eyes to the Labelins and Moger Buckley.

“I want a pony.”

In the winter of 1774–1775, Duke Henry Farway presented a plan for the purchase of the Shimmer's eyes to General Statham, the messenger of the Origins. The eye-catching holds the Council of Five, where the First is Prince Hector, and the Fourth of the Five supports him; The Farvais were going to buy up the share of Francis-Ilian in installments, and lend half a million ephesas to Origin, so that he could agree on installments with Hector and receive the rest of the reserves, so no one else could put a spark army against the northerners.

In the Gate of Trust

In February 1775, Hector is mentioned in the history of Gerion, the aide-de-camp of Francis-Ilian: after the king, having seen a prophetic dream, handed over the affairs to his son and locked himself in the monastery, most of the courtiers moved to the prince's court. Gerion, who secretly sold the secrets of his father to Hector, conceived the idea of staging the king's salvation from an assassination attempt so that he, forgetting his dreams, returned to Laam and re-occupied the throne, "knocking off" the prince.

In The Voice of Winter

The prince's offer to sell Erwin fifteen thousand spark eyes became real thanks to a loan promised by Farway. Erwin dreamed of creating in these eyes a personal select guard - kairs armed with a spark.

The “Yanmei Hunt”

Magda Labelin in Laem

When Magda Labelin came to Laam to buy eyes, Hector fed the travelers with flattery, wine and gifts for five days, but in response to her direct questions, he gave an "otherwise telling refusal": he wanted to be friends "with the great warrior, not with the loser", and the First with the Fourth of the Five sold their stocks to Origin, and the Second with the Third - to the Farway. When Magda broke out with a scathing speech about the Shimmerians, the prince raised the cup for an "unsurpassed speaker", grabbed his heart and retired with all the althes; his example was followed by the other nobles. Then the first secretary of the prince and the mercenary general Githan, on his behalf, apologized to Magda for the attack of the ship: the prince, according to them, “hurried to Faunterra at the invitation of Her Majesty”, and as a “conciliatory gift” the travelers were presented with an invoice for twenty days of residence in the palace, generously giving another four days. Gitan boasted to Colonel Horey that the young Hector would certainly befriend Origin, because "they are both favorites of the gods." Magda in retaliation tried to bribe General Lorinal Gittan, the "sword of Prince Hector", and then Colonel Horey, whom Gitane bypassed when appointed commander of the Solar Regiment. Enmity broke out between the prince and the Labelins: Magda's men were killed in Laem, her squadron attacked the Shimmerian caravan.

Request to Erwin

In May 1775, in Faunterra, Hector, together with the younger Farway, gave a speech in the House in support of the northern rebellion, clearly seeking Erwin's sympathy. (Chamber of Representatives) Erwin explained to his father that the prince would not have violated the dynasty's monopoly on the eyes if Francis-Ilian had not done the same, and the prophet was persuaded by the Farway.

Learning that his father had arrived in Marengo on the ship Lady in Darkness and wanted to regain the throne, Hector called Erwin to his quarters, where Catherine Catherine was alone with him. (Lady in the Dark) He explained that he honors his father, but can not give the throne: the father will be supported by the people who believe in his dreams, and the clergy, as well as “toads of generation” from the swamps. To kill his father, he said, would be to destroy his soul. The prince asked for half of Erwin's army to keep her in Laem under Shimmerian flags. Erwin refused ten or even five battalions, offering only one or two, but later, through a cue, Forty-Two promised military aid when needed - in exchange for a secret search for a merchant of Harmon and the Light Sphere. (Radiant Sphere) Deputy Laema Halintor indeed tried to seize the Sphere from Harmon "on the orders of His Highness", explaining that the Prince, after a conflict with Magda, whose people were killed in Laema, does not want to deal with the Labelins. Erwin, for his part, told Maurice Labelin that the prince would confirm how Magda tried to buy a huge batch of eyes from him. At Manson's trial, Erwin publicly reminded Francis-Ilian that he had asked for military assistance against his own son two weeks earlier, and Erwin refused, finding the request dishonorable.

Chamber

When the father and Manson in the trial with their heads held high moved away from the defendant's bench, Hector swore in such a loud whisper that he heard half of the Chamber. When the Duke Maurice Labelin declared war on Shimmery in the House, the prince threw a glove in his face and demanded an immediate fight; Minerva forbade the fight, and then refused and arrested the Duke, who declared war by law. In voting on the new ruler Hector, having pondered, supported Erwin:

"Origin can be trusted."

In "Humans and Gods"

In the summer of 1775, the South Route army under Magda invaded Shimmery, defeated some regiments and overbought others (the Solar Regiment passed to the Labelins), reached Pentago and captured many eyes; the kingdom lost half its wealth. Magda offered Adrian to capture Orcada and Laem, so that the prince, deprived of the capital and the army, would surrender. The king-father partly blamed the defeats on his son, who was prone to “idleness and frivolity”, but, according to him, the general anger at the Labelins reconciled them. On 1 June 1775, Francis-Ilianus told Erwin that there was "no longer any disagreement" between him and Hector, and asked for at least one battalion of kairs to help against the travelers. Later, Magda boasted to her father: “Prince Hector tried to deceive us — I took his army and eyes.”

The Shadow of the Great Tree

According to his father, Hector "showed diplomatic talent" and brought a battalion of kire to the side of Shimmeri; with him, the king and the prince returned to their homeland, restored order and punished the perpetrators of the failure. In the autumn of 1775, Hector and his father met Adrian at Soltown. At lunch, he frowned, barely complimented Karen, stopped his father, gathered in front of everyone to tell his first prophetic dream ("Father, do not need the first at the table"), and when Adrian called Erwin "a troublemaker and a rebel", objected:

“If two lands rebelled against the Lord, they could be called rebels. But if only two lands obey the Lord, the rebel is he."

The prince stated that he had drunk a cup of fraternity with Erwin and would not betray him; the Shimmerians refused to fight against the Kairs, agreeing only to cover the rear of Adrian. Next to him was Catherine Catherine Catherine, “brushed with the life of a shavanka by no means the first youth”, by that time pregnant; the king told everyone to congratulate him on his future grandson. Going north, Adrian left the Shimmerian regiments under Hector in the Southern Way - according to Magda, as a "collar" for the Labelins.

In "Fantasies"

The author warns that “Fantasies” is not a continuation of the plot, but a collection of fantasies about the possible fate of the characters.

In "Amicable" (August 1776, Laam), the thirty-three-year-old prince lives "pure honey": Catherine's wife Catherine, giving the baby to the nurse, returned to his bed; the formidable Lady in Darkness died; Alicia's highest mother took her father on church affairs to Faunterra. The prince, who wears a general's uniform for his guests, receives northerners in Laem - Jemis Lilliday and Hyder Leed - as well as Miray Nan-Claire, who asks the Solar Regiment to take power in Darkwater from Emmon Darklin, promising in return a secret fairway through the Tops of the Dark Kings. (Mireille Nen-Clair) Ambassador Darklina, on the contrary, proposes for the arrest of Miraeus the voice of Darkwater for Francis-Ilian in the election of the lord. Kairam Hector recalls that during the war he refused both the ambassadors of Stepi and Adrian, who asked for troops against Origin: “No, eat the darkness! "Origin is my friend!"; not a single Shimmerian sword has come to the North.

Hector arranges a midnight auction of altesses for the northerners at Gant Farhan, where Hyder recognizes Barney's kidnapped nephew, and then puts guests under palace arrest; introduces Jemis to his sister Demeter, his bride ("I think you are worth each other"), unsuccessfully tries to seduce Mireille and, along with Catherine, examines the consequences of the love potion that Hyder has been fermented with. In the denouement, he agrees to return Barney and give the Solar Regiment — "just not to see your blissful faces again."

In "Ad-ri-an!" (Autumn 1776) It is said that Mireille Nan-Claire persuaded the prince to give her military assistance; Erwin doubted that it was Mireille: “Hector doesn’t care about Mireille, but two hundred X’s are a serious force.” The prince is mentioned among the richest lords of the House, darkened when Minerva in her speech in the House spoke about the fact that the rulers do not know the lives of their subjects. After this story, the love of the prince and Catherine Catherine became stronger: they cheated on each other no more than once a year, which for the South is considered an exceptional fidelity.

Relationships

Francis-Ilian

Father and son were competing for power. Hector bought his father's secrets from his aide-de-camp, Gerion; his father, in his own words, traced the thread. In 1775, the prince was afraid that his father would “see in a dream” that Hector had been overthrown, and the people would take it for God’s will. The war with the Labelins brought them closer together.

Erwin Origin

Erwin called Hector a friend, and the prince his "lovely" friend and drinking companion. Their friendship withstood Erwin's refusal to give an army, and Adrian's pressure: Hector refused to fight against the Kairs.

Catherine Catherine

A Westerner born in Halliwell and sold to the South; was an altess of a Shimmer merchant, a mayor, then a prince. By 1774, she became Adrian's adviser on secular intrigue, and in the war with the Steppe Fire, she returned to Hector. In Shadow of the Great Tree, she is his "fairy althessa" expecting a child, in Fantasies, his son's wife and mother, calling herself "still the niece of the ganta Cort". She is clever and mocking (in a conversation with Erwin, she “smiled with one eye”), and in Fantasies she is shown as a subtle politician jealous only “strategically”. For more information, see Catherine Catherine.

Personality and Appearance

A handsome man with black (“resin”) hair, a strand of which falls on the right eye, so that the pupil “blows through it, as if from an ambush”; brown eyes. In the war, he wore a white enamel breastplate, a snow cape with silver moons and a horned helmet polished to a mirror shine. Self-absorbed, theatrical, loves luxury, pleasure and the southern Nega (in his rooms there is always pulling music and girls in transparent silks), is cruel and indifferent to other people's deaths. At the same time, he knows how to maintain friendship and does not like blood: “We do not solve matters with blood. We don’t like death, grief, women’s cry.”

Appearances

  • "Only One Star" - first time in Manson's chapter; Battle of Orange.
  • "A Doll on the Throne" - the interrogation of Neymir and Chara, the defeat at the Rain Forest, a visit to the court of Minerva.
  • "I want a pony" is a reference in Farway's plan to purchase eyes.
  • The Gate of Trust is a reference in the history of Gerion. (The Gates of Trust)
  • "The Voice of Winter" - refers to his offer to sell 15 thousand eyes.
  • "Yanmei Hunt" - Magda in Laem, request to Erwin, Chamber. (The Yanmei Hunt)
  • "The Shadow of the Great Tree" - Soltown.
  • "Fantasies" - "Fantasy Fifth: Amicable"; mentions in "Ad-ri-an!".

Trivia

  • In the 2026 edition of Arrow, Coin, Spark, Prince Hector sits with a pair of violass on the grandstand during the military parade at Faunterra on the day of June 24, 1774. In early media outlets, he was replaced by a Shimmerian king with a crown prince.
  • One of Hector's sisters, like the relatives of the other members of the Council of Five, possesses the secret of cutting battle eyes.
  • In Fantasia, Hector envied his sister Demeter, who lived alone in his father's palace among the waterfalls, and tried to move her to arrange a "nest" there for love pleasure.
